shape-2 BAR (written 2026-10-03 before any box run of shape-2). Question: shape-1 compared C-driver and stock-torch tokens over 32 greedy tokens (100/100 equal); do they still agree token for token when the decoded string is four times longer (128 tokens) on a larger prompt set, on the same Llama shape the C driver was never pinned on? Model: JackFram/llama-160m converted to bf16 (model.safetensors sha256 261167a02cc8283b0a081b707ccabbf6ad8738d83bfe1b149d0b86d11391cfc4; hidden 768, 12 layers, 12 heads with 12 KV heads, untied lm_head, vocab 32000; config.json carries rope_theta 10000.0 explicitly, sha256 0ad6a8dd8d2f724972df9b5213d24cc4280f59f3da95d16fe0f878b40c7db675). Prompts: 300 = the 200 sv-5 TEST prompts then the 100 sv-5 CAL prompts, re-tokenised from their text with the llama tokenizer, BOS included, cut at 64 tokens (prompts.jsonl sha256 7abda01bdbff527b0e220a790688c186a9a6f2424947e7be7643b2a4f4840c6c; the CAL ones carry the label "test" only because the driver's split filter needs one; idx 0..99 are byte-identical to shape-1 prompts); 128 greedy tokens; one run per prompt. Reference: stock PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu fp32 greedy decoding on the bf16-widened weights, 1 thread, KV cache, built on penguin before any box run (ref128.jsonl sha256 9487f81dc5f0bbd51f0d0805f988e8e38f8cf92e863197f1d2a202a5914385d6; its first 32 tokens equal the shape-1 reference on 100/100). Driver: ~/sv5/arma/verify3/sv5_driver built with the spec flags, run by shape2_job.sh (sha256 8212767758fbe4ac29d6074b9d2789b53453bc5163e05f39de3949ff84a52fc6). Hosts: box4 (Sempron SI-42, SSE3 only) and box5 (Pentium T2310, SSSE3 only) through the feed; penguin (AVX2) as a unit.
(b) HEADLINE, own verdict: MET only if the C driver's whole 128-token string equals the torch string on at least 294 of 300 prompts (98 %), on EACH of box4 and box5. 293 or fewer on either box = NOT MET. Reasoning for the threshold: shape-1 saw 0 differences in 3,200 compared positions and a 10-prompt x 128 penguin smoke test saw 0 in 1,280, so a 95 % bar would be near-certain; 98 % asks whether exact agreement survives the longer decode, where one near-tied argmax between two different fp32 summation orders would split the rest of the string.
(a) SECONDARY, reported but not the headline (near-certain by design: same binary, pinned arithmetic): MET only if box4, box5 and penguin give identical ids_out, witness digest and argmax digest on 300 of 300 prompts. If the penguin rows are missing at recording time, (a) is reported for box4 vs box5 only and labelled so.
Prediction written before the run: (b) MET with 296 to 300 of 300 on each box (a smoke run on penguin: 10 of 10); (a) yes. Reported without a bar: first differing position and idx for every prompt where C and torch disagree, whether such prompts are in the TEST or the CAL part, first-32-token agreement with the shape-1 rows on idx 0..99, seconds per prompt per host. Scope: one model shape, one prompt set, 128 tokens; says nothing about larger models, other tokenizers, bias/GQA architectures, or throughput. A negative outcome is reported as negative.
title: CIS-2 C driver on llama-160m at 128 greedy tokens (300 prompts): agreement with stock torch fp32 on box4/box5, digests across three CPU classes

summary: MET on the headline (b): the C driver (sv5_driver, gcc -O2 build fb7ec824...) on BF16 llama-160m weights gives the same whole 128-token greedy output as stock PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu fp32 on 300 of 300 prompts on box4 (Sempron, SSE3) and 300 of 300 on box5 (Pentium T2310, SSSE3); pass needs 294 on each. Independent verifier recounted from the raw rows with its own script (whole-list equality of exactly 128 ids), confirmed 300 distinct prompts per box, no early stop (no EOS in any of 600 outputs), prompts/reference/weights hashes equal to the pass mark, reference built by PyTorch without the driver and before the box jobs. Secondary (a): ids, witness and argmax fields identical between box4 and box5 on 300 of 300 rows; the penguin (AVX2) unit was NOT run, so (a) covers the two boxes only. Caveats: one model shape (llama-160m), one number format, benign prompts of at most 64 tokens, greedy, one run per prompt; about 5% of outputs are repetitive (1 of 300 is a single repeated token, 16 have a short periodic tail), which makes those matches easy; this shows equal token strings, not bit-identical logits against PyTorch; no throughput claim; the driver hash is pinned by earlier sv-5 records, not in this pass mark; the reference logs are empty, so the PyTorch version rests on the venv and the pass-mark text.
